event_overview.title: About Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine conflict is the ongoing interstate war centered on Russia’s military actions against Ukraine, including the full-scale invasion launched on February 24, 2022, against a backdrop of Russia’s actions in and against Ukraine since 2014. It has involved sustained combat, long-range missile and drone attacks, humanitarian disruption, and international diplomatic, legal, and sanctions responses.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: Russia’s full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022; international institutions also treat the wider situation as encompassing events in Ukraine from 2013-14 onward.

facts.label: Location and parties
facts.value: The conflict is fought primarily on and over Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, involving Russia and Ukraine; the UN General Assembly has repeatedly reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within those borders.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: The UN General Assembly’s March 2, 2022 resolution characterized Russia’s actions as aggression against Ukraine and demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its military forces.

facts.label: International criminal investigation
facts.value: The International Criminal Court opened its Ukraine investigation on March 2, 2022. Its stated scope covers alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide committed by any person on any part of Ukraine’s territory from November 21, 2013 onward.

facts.label: Humanitarian dimension
facts.value: The war has produced a major humanitarian and displacement emergency; UNHCR describes the February 2022 escalation as one of the fastest-growing displacement emergencies in recent history.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major late-July and early-August 2026 military, diplomatic and cross-border developments connected to the war; it does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict’s battlefield, humanitarian, political or legal history.

explore_lenses.label: How did the ceasefire reach this impasse?
explore_lenses.title: Phase two stalled over disarmament and withdrawal
explore_lenses.summary: The dispute centers on the unfinished second phase of the October 2025 ceasefire. The UN-endorsed framework links a staged Israeli withdrawal to Gaza’s demilitarization, an international stabilization force and a civilian Palestinian transition.

claims.text: The UN-endorsed plan says Israeli forces would progressively hand territory to an International Stabilization Force, with complete withdrawal tied to agreed demilitarization standards, milestones and timeframes; it also contemplates a residual security perimeter until Gaza is assessed as secure.
Nine months after the U.S.-brokered ceasefire was signed, negotiations had largely deadlocked over phase two, including Hamas disarmament and Gaza’s reconstruction.

UN officials have said the plan’s major elements are interdependent: Hamas and other armed groups’ disarmament, Israeli withdrawal, deployment of the stabilization force and enabling the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza to take transitional responsibilities.

Hamas’ stated condition is that disarmament belongs within a broader political package, including confidence that Israel will implement its side; Israel defines demilitarization broadly, extending from heavier weapons to tens of thousands of rifles.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is an ongoing armed conflict that began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel carried out strikes in Iran and Iran subsequently attacked U.S. military assets and regional states. It has expanded beyond direct military exchanges to include disputes over maritime access in the Strait of Hormuz, ceasefire efforts, and risks to commercial shipping and civilian seafarers.

facts.label: Start and principal belligerents
facts.value: The United Nations reported that U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran occurred on February 28, 2026; Iran then targeted U.S. military assets and attacks affected several regional states. In a subsequent Security Council letter, the United States said it had commenced combat operations against Iran that day in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: A central theater is the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway between Iran and Oman linking the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. The conflict has also affected U.S. forces and states across the Gulf region.

facts.label: Maritime and legal dimension
facts.value: The International Maritime Organization has treated attacks on merchant shipping and restrictions on passage through Hormuz as a major international-shipping issue. Its Council stated that transit passage through straits used for international navigation must not be threatened, impeded, denied, or suspended, and that any traffic measures must accord with IMO rules and international law.

facts.label: Diplomatic framework
facts.value: Ceasefire and mediation efforts have occurred alongside renewed fighting. The UN described a June 17 memorandum of understanding and Qatar-facilitated implementation talks, while warning in early July that the arrangement remained fragile after further U.S.-Iran confrontations.

facts.label: Civilian shipping impact
facts.value: IMO said on June 15 that it had verified at least 46 attacks on international shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began, and it later organized a voluntary emergency framework to help vessels and seafarers confined in the Gulf depart safely.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July 2026 escalation involving U.S. threats and strikes, congressional war-powers action, Houthi-linked developments, oil-market disruption, and a reported pause in attacks; it does not provide a complete record of the war’s origins, all regional operations, or the full course of diplomacy.

explore_lenses.label: How did Hormuz become the central issue?
explore_lenses.title: War and attacks choked a vital shipping route
explore_lenses.summary: The route dispute emerged from the conflict that began on February 28, then intensified as threats and attacks on shipping sharply reduced traffic. The stakes extend beyond the parties to the war because the strait had carried a major share of global oil and gas flows.
